matched_finding.subcategory: Hypothesis 2 indirect effect does not match the reported path product
matched_finding.description: Hypothesis 2 indirect effect does not match the reported path product: The point estimate for Hypothesis 2 should match the product of the two displayed paths. The text reports .26 for T2 experienced patient incivility predicting T3 negative emotions and .37 for T3 negative emotions predicting T4 compassion fatigue. Their product is .096, which would round to .10; even with ordinary two-decimal rounding, this product cannot be .07. If the MPlus constraint used different coefficients, those coefficients need to be shown. Otherwise, revise the indirect estimate and its SE/CI from the same model. As written, readers cannot tell which mediation path was tested.
matched_finding.quote: We then used MPlus' model constraint feature to estimate the indirect path $a \times d$. In support of Hypothesis 2, the positive indirect relationship between experienced patient incivility and compassion fatigue through negative emotions was significant $(\mathrm{B}=.07, \mathrm{SE}=.03, \mathrm{p}<.05,95 \% \mathrm{Cl}[0.02,0.14])$.

matched_finding.subcategory: Dropped autoregressive controls in supplemental analysis
matched_finding.description: Dropped autoregressive controls in supplemental analysis: The relative-importance analysis may not be directly comparable to the autoregressive mediation model. The description says enacted incivility was regressed on experienced incivility, negative emotions, and compassion fatigue, with no mention of the Time 1 autoregressive or work-hour controls used in the main analyses. If those controls were omitted, the reported 45.1%/30.8%/24.1% variance shares describe a different, less-adjusted model rather than the variance decomposition of the main longitudinal model.
matched_finding.quote: Because regression only provides information on how much scores a given outcome change following a single unit change in a given predictor, we conducted a relative importance analysis to understand the proportion of variance each predictor accounts for in enacted incivility (Tonidandel \& LeBreton, 2011). First, using the native $\operatorname{lm}()$ function in $R$ ( $R$ Core Team, 2021), we regressed enacted incivility on predictors from this stage--experienced incivility ( $\mathrm{B}=-.03$, $\mathrm{SE}=.04, \mathrm{p}=.40$ ), negative emotions ( $\mathrm{B}=.23, \mathrm{SE}=.04, \mathrm{p}<.001$ ), and compassion fatigue ( $\mathrm{B}=.23$, $\mathrm{SE}=.04, \mathrm{p}<.001$ ).

matched_finding.subcategory: Repeated nurse-patient contact is ruled out more strongly than the data allow
matched_finding.description: Repeated nurse-patient contact is ruled out more strongly than the data allow: The paper identifies repeated contact with the same patient as a possible alternative pathway, but then dismisses it too firmly. A handoff rate from “some nursing units” and a national mean length of stay for all hospitals do not establish the recurrence rate in this sample. The 6.1-day average is also close to the one-week survey interval and says nothing about the upper tail of patient stays. Nurses can have sustained interactions with the same patients or family members within shifts or across consecutive days. Since patient identities were not tracked, the safer conclusion is that repeated dyadic encounters could not be evaluated here; handoffs and work schedules may make them less common in some units, but they cannot be excluded. The argument would be more convincing if the transience claim were tied more clearly to the study’s weekly, future-customer focus rather than to customer interactions generally.
matched_finding.quote: In combination with condensed 3 -day work weeks (Merrifield, 2017) and an average length of stay for all hospitals at 6.1 days (CDC, 2016), the likelihood that participants would be treating the same patients at multiple time points is very unlikely.

matched_finding.subcategory: CFA reporting in Analytic Strategy is hard to reconcile
matched_finding.description: CFA reporting in Analytic Strategy is hard to reconcile: The CFA paragraph appears to mix or insufficiently label absolute model-fit statistics and chi-square difference-test statistics. The degrees of freedom reported for the three-, two-, and one-factor alternatives are not plausible as absolute CFA model degrees of freedom, while RMSEA, CFI, and TLI are reported alongside them as if they were ordinary model-fit indices. This makes the discriminant-validity evidence difficult to evaluate as written.
matched_finding.quote: Before evaluating our hypotheses, we investigated the discriminant validity of our measures by employing a series of confirmatory factor analyses. First, we assessed our hypothesized four-factor model absent of the temporal control measures. We applied procedures recommended by Nye and Drasgow (2011) to model the data at the item-level using WLSMV in MPlus 8.0. The fit of the four-factor model was acceptable $(269)=862.05$, RMSEA $=.08$, CFI $=.99$, TLI $=$ .99) and fit the data better than a three-factor model wherein both incivility measures were set to load onto the same factor $(3)=82.52$, RMSEA $=.09$, CFI $=.98$, TLI $=.98$ ), a two-factor model wherein both incivility measures were loaded onto one factor and negative emotions towards patients and compassion fatigue were loaded onto the second factor (2) $=82.65, \mathrm{RMSEA}=.10, \mathrm{CFI}=.98, \mathrm{TLI}=.98$ ), and a one-factor model (1) $=8.02, \mathrm{RMSEA}=.10, \mathrm{CFI}=.98, \mathrm{TLI}=.98$ ).

matched_finding.subcategory: Missing-data handling is unclear before Results
matched_finding.description: Missing-data handling is unclear before Results: The missing-data discussion notes that perceived patient acuity had missing or invalid responses, but it does not state how many cases were affected or how missingness was handled analytically. This matters because the final sample is N=372, whereas the main mediation tables use N=321 and the moderation table uses N=244, apparently due to moderator missingness. Table 3 explains its smaller N as due to moderator missingness, but the reduction to N=321 for the descriptive correlations and main mediation regressions is not explained. Unless this reflects a clearly defined complete-case analytic sample or another missing-data decision, the discrepancy leaves the effective sample size for the main results unclear. The analytic samples and missing-data treatment should be clearer for interpreting the moderation and mediation results.
matched_finding.quote:
Finally, our perceived patient acuity measure had missing data. For missing cases, responses were either left blank ( $55 \%$ of missing values were due to no-response) or the value provided was outside of the expected numerical range ( $45 \%$ of missing values were due to an incorrect response). However, a comparison of personal demographics and workplace characteristics did not find any significant differences between participants with and without missing values for perceived patient acuity.
